hooks.text: A city-bus-sized asteroid snuck halfway inside our Moon's protective orbit.
Did a city-bus-sized asteroid almost strike Earth without warning?
A city-bus-sized rock passed one hundred seventy-five thousand kilometers from Earth.

title: The Asteroid That Snuck Inside the Moon
description: Discover how a city-bus-sized asteroid named 2023 DZ2 was found just weeks before passing closer than the Moon.

beats.text: In February 2023, astronomers at a Canary Islands observatory spotted an unexpected visitor heading toward Earth.
beats.visual: photograph of Isaac Newton Telescope exterior, La Palma, 2023
subjects: Observatorio de Roque de los Muchachos

beats.text: Initial estimates showed a rock forty to ninety meters across, orbiting the Sun every three years.
beats.visual: diagram of Apollo asteroid orbit, NASA, 2023

beats.text: Worse yet, orbital calculations briefly flagged the object as a virtual impactor for March 2026.
Alarm spread until further radar tracking completely ruled out any impact, removing it from threat lists.
beats.visual: photograph of Goldstone antenna dish, NASA, 2023
queries: Goldstone Deep Space Communications Complex antenna

beats.text: On March 25, the fast-rotating space rock zoomed past at one hundred seventy-five thousand kilometers.
beats.visual: photograph of Earth and Moon from space true color, NASA, 2023
queries: Earth and Moon from space true color

beats.text: It missed Earth by just half the Moon's distance, merely weeks after humans first noticed it.
beats.visual: artist's concept of near Earth object passing Earth, NASA, 2023

beats.text: Astronomers were relieved that nothing struck before this close flyby.
